description: Per-conflict lifecycle state machine. Mirrors docs/concepts/FLOWS.md::Conflict resolution. The enforcement table in internal/conflicts/service.go::canTransition is the runtime authority; flow-verifier replays this declaration to assert agreement.

states.name: detected
states.description: Conflict was emitted by a detector and persisted with status=detected.

states.name: assigned
states.description: Operator assigned the conflict to a target domain.

states.name: split
states.description: Conflict was split into per-domain sub-conflicts.

states.name: resolved
states.description: Conflict resolution has been recorded (apply still required for file movement).

states.name: validated
states.description: Resolved conflict has been validated against a fresh detection run.

states.name: committed
states.description: Validated resolution has been committed to the repo via apply.

states.name: force_resolved
states.description: Operator explicitly chose to ignore the conflict (force-resolve).

transitions.guard: operator marks resolved without explicit assign
deferred to v0.2 (apply is unimplemented in v0.1)

invariants: Only the apply phase moves a conflict from 'validated' to 'committed'; v0.1 cannot reach 'committed'.
Reopen is allowed from any non-initial, non-terminal state.
notes: Adding a new state or transition requires (1) updating canTransition in internal/conflicts/service.go, (2) updating this contract, (3) running `flow-verifier verify check` and `flow-verifier verify replay`. Without flow-verifier wired in this scenario yet (see docs/operations/RUNBOOK.md::Bootstrap flow-verifier when missing), the contract is read-only documentation. Phase 10 plans wire the verifier.
